newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai crusher buys Aug soybeans, corn import agreed.
newsitem.headline: Thai crusher buys Aug soybeans, corn import agreed.

text.p: Thai feedmills scrambled to buy after the government finally approved imports of 150,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn, trade sources said on Tuesday.
One major oil crusher was said to have just bought 30,000 tonnes of Argentine soybeans for August shipment, they said. Price details were not known.
Traders said some feedmills who anticipated the government's go-ahead to the corn imports had started buying last week.

"Most will have to buy cargoes in transit. Argentine corn costs around $135 per tonne c&f Si Chang. With cargoes in transit, we might have to add around $10-per-tonne premiums," said a Bangkok-based trader.
The Thai cabinet on Tuesday gave a green light to the industry to import 150,000 tonnes of zero tariff corn to alleviate a shortage caused by a dry spell.
The corn must be imported by August 31 as local supplies were expected to be available by then.
The government estimated the unseasonably late rainy season would cut corn output for 1997/98 July-June) to 3.16-3.62 million tonnes from more than four million seen earlier.
It projected the shortage during July and August at around 175,950-198,550 tonnes.
The corn shortage pushed prices up to 5.20 baht per kg this week while they barely rise above 4.50 under normal circumstances.
The government earlier approved 200,000 tonnes of corn imports under a similar scheme.
The soymeal market was quiet with only modest buying as the industry was sidelined by rising prices.
"Players can sit back and wait for better conditions, be it prices or currency value as many of them have two/three months of stock," said a trader at a major US trading house.
Traders said the industry was encouraged by the upward movement of the baht as it broke through the 32 per dollar level on expectations the IMF will step in soon to revive the economy.

"If sentiment continues to improve, we hope we'll see the 30 baht per dollar level again soon. That will be the level that buyers will be more comfortable to enter the market," said another trader. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
